annotations.text:
DIRECTION: the desk's own palette and typefaces, at prose scale.
A stranger sees the instrument they will actually get, not a bright marketing page followed by a black terminal.

Copy is co-owned with Marketing. Placement findings go back to it rather than getting trimmed in place, and never two seats in one file at once.

THIS PAGE SHIPS FIRST NOW - the split reversed it.

Google needs a public home page that describes the app and links to privacy and terms. So / becomes the landing page and the board moves to /desk, keeping the password it has because the server default still denies there.

Deferred instead: /signin and /auth/. Opening /signin early is how the first stranger through the door takes the authority to spend his money.

A LIST OF ONE, not one button centred.
The group, its label and the stack all survive a second provider arriving; the second row is not drawn.

Google's button is used to Google's spec and not restyled to the desk — a restyled one is a verification risk and reads as a fake.

SIX SIGN-IN STATES, EACH WITH THE STATUS CODE IT MUST SEND.
Only one offers 'try again', and only because its wall is a clock rather than a decision.

The seventh card is kept deliberately - it drew refusal as a sign-in outcome, which was wrong, and the wrong assumption is the useful part.

SIGNED IN, NOT ADMITTED.
Invite-only makes this reachable the day enforcement ships. A person here has a session and an account row - not a stranger.

SETTLED 2026-09-11: refusal happens at the point of use, so sign-in refuses nobody - it creates the row as pending and succeeds. The status check must live in ONE place every point of use passes through.
